tellings.difference: Names Sarfatti as the one who got the call, dates it to the 1950s rather than the 1970s, frames the caller as from the future, and says the voice told him he would meet the others and work on building UFOs.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of a phone call from a strange voice, presumably alien or from the future, which matches Sarfatti's well-known childhood call. The match is uncertain because the stored telling does not name who got the call.

plain: A scientist is said to have picked up the phone and heard a metallic voice, some kind of alien intelligence, speaking to him. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells it briefly on the show, without naming where he got it, and places it in the 1970s. Jesse Michels tells a fuller version. He names the man who got the call as the physicist Jack Sarfatti and puts the call in the 1950s. In his telling the voice came from the future and told Sarfatti he would meet "the others" and would end up working on, as Michels puts it, "building UFOs essentially." Michels credits a book called The Hippies Saved Physics, and he mentions the names Hal Puthoff, Hans Bethe and David Kaiser alongside it. If true, it would mean that some unknown intelligence reached out to steer a young scientist toward exotic physics.
